QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_1

question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, a Cat III AIF, plans to appoint a new external member 'Dr. Arvind Rao' to its Investment Committee whose name was NOT disclosed in the PPM. The fund has 20 investors with total value of investment of INR 400 crore. Consent from investors representing INR 325 crore by value of investment has been received. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, can Dr. Rao be validly appointed?

answer.text: No, because less than 75% of investors by NUMBER (15 out of 20 required) have consented.
Yes, because consent representing 81.25% of investors by value of investment has been received, exceeding the 75% threshold.
No, because all 100% of investors must consent for a new external IC member post-onboarding.
Yes, because the manager's own decision is sufficient for external member appointments.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI requires that external IC members whose names were NOT disclosed in the PPM at on-boarding can be appointed only with consent of at least 75 percent of investors BY VALUE OF INVESTMENT. Here, INR 325 cr / INR 400 cr = 81.25%, which crosses the 75% value-weighted threshold. Hence the appointment is valid. The Trap: One distractor confuses the test with 'by number of investors' — the SEBI test is explicitly 'by value of investment'. Another invents a 100% unanimity rule that does not exist. Another ignores the mandatory investor consent requirement for undisclosed external IC members. Note: Page 277 of the workbook states the 75% consent threshold is measured by value of investment, not by number of investors or by commitments.
